title: arXiv Physics — notable papers in the 27 October 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this is an inferred notable-paper ordering based on expert picks and checkable scientific/publication signals, with little usable citation evidence for such recent work.

sections.title: Latest arXiv Physics batch: 27 October 2026
sections.text: Seven selected papers from 1,088 deduplicated entries. The strongest recurring pattern is neutrino astrophysics spanning MeV, PeV, and EeV scales.

sections.title: Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background
sections.authors: The Super-Kamiokande Collaboration; K. Abe, Y. Asaoka, M. Harada, Y. Hayato, K. Hiraide, et al.
sections.abstract: An analysis of 5,003.0 days of Super-Kamiokande data reports an indication of diffuse supernova-background electron antineutrinos using improved atmospheric-neutrino rejection and updated systematics.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a best-fit flux of 3.6 +1.6/−1.5 cm⁻² s⁻¹ above 13.3 MeV and a 2.6σ (one-sided 99.5% C.L.) tension with the null hypothesis.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; Super-Kamiokande 5003.0-day water/Gd-water data and a spectral fit against six backgrounds
sections.unique_caveat: The spectral-fit significance is not a discovery; the complementary model-independent count analysis gives 1.8σ, and the inferred flux depends on signal and background modeling.

sections.title: Observation of the T_cbarc1(4430)- state in B0 to D*- D0 K+ decays
sections.authors: LHCb Collaboration; R. Aaij, M. Abdelfatah, A.S.W. Abdelmotteleb, C. Abellan Beteta, F. Abudinén, et al.
sections.abstract: An amplitude analysis of LHCb proton-proton collision data finds that adding the T_cbarc1(4430)- state improves the description of the B0 to D*- D0 K+ data with significance above 5σ.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report the first observation of T_cbarc1(4430)- to D*- D0; the paper’s amplitude analysis gives 5.3σ after its assessed systematic uncertainties.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; LHCb amplitude analysis of 9 fb-1 of proton-proton data at center-of-mass energies 7, 8, and 13 TeV
sections.unique_caveat: The internal structure of the state remains unresolved; the amplitude model and its systematic variations matter, and the result does not distinguish molecular, compact-tetraquark, or kinematic interpretations.

sections.title: The design and flight of the Payload for Ultrahigh Energy Observations (PUEO)
sections.authors: PUEO Collaboration; Q. Abarr, S. Agarwal, J. Alfaro, S. Ali, P. Allison, et al.
sections.abstract: The PUEO Collaboration describes the design, construction, and as-built validation of a balloon-borne antenna array intended to detect Askaryan radio emission from ultrahigh-energy neutrinos interacting in Antarctic ice.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a successful 23-day Antarctic balloon flight in January 2026 and describe the payload’s instrument, calibration, navigation, and first-look flight performance.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; NASA PUEO balloon payload, preflight tests, in-flight calibration and performance data
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports no neutrino flux or detection. The authors report an average duty cycle near 55% (about 12 days 21 hours of livetime), with thermal and downstream data-throughput limits affecting operations.

sections.title: PeV Diffuse Neutrinos from Magnetically Arrested Disks in Low-Luminosity Active Galactic Nuclei
sections.abstract: The authors model all-flavor diffuse neutrino emission from magnetically arrested accretion flows in low-luminosity active galactic nuclei and constrain the source fraction using current IceCube data.
sections.claimed_result: With 5% of accretion power assigned to nonthermal protons, the authors infer that at most 2.3×10⁻³ of LLAGNs can host the relevant MAD state; an assumed MAD fraction of about 1.6×10⁻³ gives a modeled intensity peak near 1.5 PeV.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; diffuse-flux and neutrino-cascade modeling for pp and pγ production, constrained by IceCube observations
sections.unique_caveat: These are model-dependent source-population limits, not an identified neutrino source; the allowed fraction changes with the assumed proton energy budget and LLAGN/LERG population relation.

sections.title: Yb/Sr optical clock comparison at 2.2E-18 uncertainty over a 1350-km fiber link
sections.authors: Lei Hou, Xiang-Pei Liu, Zhuan-Xian Xiong, Fa-Xi Chen, Wen-Xuan Song, et al.
sections.abstract: A phase-stabilized 1350-km fiber link is used to compare ytterbium and strontium optical lattice clocks in Wuhan and Shanghai at 2.18×10⁻¹⁸ total uncertainty.
sections.claimed_result: The authors give a Yb/Sr frequency ratio of 1.207 507 039 343 337 716 0(26), with 1.14×10⁻¹⁸ Bayesian statistical and 2.18×10⁻¹⁸ total uncertainty, and report a correlation with Earth tides.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; two optical lattice clocks compared over a phase-stabilized 1350-km fiber link
sections.unique_caveat: This is one clock pair and one intercity link; it demonstrates network capability but does not establish repeatability across a wider clock network.

sections.title: Direct measurement of the 23Mg(p,gamma)24Al reaction using the DRAGON recoil separator and a hybrid array of gamma-ray detectors
sections.authors: A. C. Edwin, G. Christian, A. Lennarz, I. Casandjian, S. M. Collins, et al.
sections.abstract: A direct inverse-kinematics measurement with a radioactive magnesium beam constrains the resonance strength and energy that dominate this reaction at classical nova temperatures.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report resonance strength ωγ = 38(7) meV and energy Ecm = 478.8(26) keV; their rate calculation is constrained to a 1σ up/down factor of 1.5 or smaller at 0.2–0.4 GK.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; radioactive 23Mg beam, DRAGON recoil separator, and coincident LaBr3/CeBr3/BGO gamma-ray detectors
sections.unique_caveat: The stated rate constraint covers the nova-temperature range studied and depends on rate calculations; it does not remove model uncertainties in other stellar environments or other reaction channels.

sections.title: Observation of measurement-induced localization phenomena in a solid-state spin system
sections.authors: Haolin Zhang, Shaoyi Xu, Zihang Zheng, Mengqi Wang, Mingzhe Liu, et al.
sections.abstract: Experiments on interacting 13C nuclear spins in diamond find longer spin autocorrelation times as projective or global weak-measurement frequency increases, consistent with measurement-induced localization.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report substantially prolonged spin autocorrelation times with increasing measurement frequency and interpret this, together with simulations, as evidence for a localized regime.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; interacting 13C nuclear-spin system in diamond, with numerical simulations
sections.unique_caveat: The measured autocorrelation response is evidence for localization, not a direct measurement of entanglement scaling or a full thermodynamic phase transition.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.text: Neutrino astrophysics across MeV, PeV, and EeV scales; precision analyses and instrumentation; quantum control in atomic-clock and solid-state-spin systems; an isolated open-charm spectroscopy result.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.text: Test the DSNB indication with more Gd-enhanced exposure and independent background models; use IceCube-Gen2 to test the LLAGN/MAD PeV prediction; improve PUEO thermal and sustained data throughput; discriminate open-charm hadron interpretations with larger samples; replicate long-distance clock results across links; and measure entanglement-sensitive observables in the diamond-spin system.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The clearest shared story is neutrino astrophysics pursued through complementary evidence: a tentative MeV-scale indication, a conditional PeV source model, and an EeV-capable Antarctic payload. Separately, LHCb reports a >5σ open-charm decay observation; the other results remain bounded by their stated models, systematics, or single-platform scope.
